answer: Each identity must complete a fresh, continuous chain of modular squarings, with each result required to compute the next; a Wesolowski proof can verify the completed delay compactly. An attacker may run separate chains in parallel, but cannot divide one chain among GPUs to eliminate its sequential latency. Creating many clones therefore requires parallel hardware or repeated real-time work, imposing a physical cost rather than allowing identities to appear instantly. Quill, onyx, and lantern can serve as distinct challenge labels, not shortcuts around that cost.
